commitResults.messageTitle: Organize classes into jamal and jamal.task packages
commitResults.messageBody:
Move the six classes out of the default package so the project has a
proper package structure, as required by the A-Packages increment.
src/main/java remains the source root.

The task data model (Task, Todo, Deadline, Event) goes into jamal.task
because those four are the part of the program that would survive a
rewrite of the chatbot around them. The entry point (JamaL) and the
user-facing exception (JamaLException) stay in jamal as app-level code.

JamaL.java imports the four task classes explicitly rather than with a
wildcard, so what crosses the package boundary is visible at a glance.
No class bodies changed: Task was already public with public accessors,
so the split needed no visibility edits.

Note: the IntelliJ run configuration main class must be updated from
JamaL to jamal.JamaL.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add saving and loading of tasks
Extract Ui, Parser, TaskList and Command classes
commitResults.messageBody:
JamaL handled input, parsing, storage calls and printing in one class,
which made each part hard to change on its own.

Split the responsibilities:
* Ui reads input and prints every reply
* Parser turns a line of input into a Command
* TaskList owns the tasks and the index checks
* Command subclasses each perform one action

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject | in task text and handle blank input
commitResults.messageBody:
A task whose text contained "|" saved fine, but on the next start the
save file had too many fields on that line, so the task was dropped as
a broken line. Reject "|" when the task is created instead.

A blank line produced "I'm not doing whatever  is.", which reads like
a bug. Reply with a proper prompt instead.

Also wrap two Storage comment lines that sat at the 120-character hard
limit of the coding standard.
